title: Chicken tikka traybake with chickpeas, spinach and mint raita

shared.display: 300 g (half for the marinade, half for the raita)

flexible.cook_note: Boil brown basmati for 25 min; microwave cauliflower rice for 3 min.

steps: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Put the rice on now if you're having it.
Mix 150 g of the yoghurt with the garlic, ginger, spices, half the lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Stir in the chicken to coat.
Toss the onion, peppers and chickpeas with the oil on a large roasting tray. Nestle the chicken on top.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until the chicken is cooked through and charred at the edges.
Meanwhile make the raita: mix the remaining yoghurt with the cucumber, mint, the rest of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Stir the spinach through the hot tray until it wilts, about 2 minutes.
Plate using the plating guide. Box the lunch portions once cooled, keeping the raita separate.
reheat_note: Microwave for 2-3 minutes until piping hot. Keep the raita separate and add it after reheating.

title: Thai green chicken curry with green beans and edamame

flexible.cook_note: Boil brown basmati for 25 min; microwave cauliflower rice for 3 min.

steps: Start the rice if you're having it.
Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat. Fry the curry paste, garlic and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until sealed all over.
Pour in the coconut milk and fish sauce, bring to a simmer, then add the green beans, pepper and courgette. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the edamame for the last 3 minutes. Check the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the lime juice and most of the coriander. Taste and add more fish sauce if needed.
Plate using the plating guide, topped with toasted cashews and the rest of the coriander.
reheat_note: Microwave for 2-3 minutes, stirring halfway, until piping hot. Pack the cashews separately so they stay crunchy.

title: Smoky turkey and two-bean chilli

shared.display: 1 cube, made up with 200 ml water

flexible.cook_note: Boil brown basmati for 25 min; microwave cauliflower rice for 3 min.

steps: Heat the oil in a large casserole. Soften the onion and peppers for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Turn up the heat, add the turkey mince and brown it, breaking it up with a spoon, for 5 minutes.
Stir in the spices and tomato puree for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and both beans. Simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes until thick. Season to taste.
Meanwhile cook the rice if you're having it.
Plate using the plating guide and top with grated cheddar.
reheat_note: Microwave for 3 minutes, stirring halfway, until piping hot. Freezes well for up to 3 months.

title: Chicken fajita bowls with black beans, avocado and lime yoghurt

flexible.cook_note: Warm wraps in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side.

steps: Toss the chicken with the spices, garlic, half the oil and a pinch of salt.
Heat the rest of the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Cook the peppers and onion for 5 minutes until charred, then tip onto a plate.
Cook the chicken in the same pan for 6-8 minutes until cooked through. Return the veg, add the black beans and half the lime juice, and warm through.
Mix the yoghurt with the rest of the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Build bowls: lettuce and tomatoes, then the chicken mix, avocado, lime yoghurt and coriander. Add wraps or rice per the plating guide.
reheat_note: Good cold as a salad bowl. To eat warm, microwave the chicken and beans only. Pack the salad, yoghurt and avocado separately (squeeze lime over the avocado).

title: Ginger beef and broccoli stir-fry

flexible.cook_note: Cook noodles per the pack (about 5 min); boil brown basmati for 25 min.

steps: Mix the soy sauce, rice vinegar, chilli flakes and sesame oil in a jug.
Cook the noodles or rice if you're having them. Drain the noodles and toss with a splash of the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok until smoking. Stir-fry the beef in two batches for 2 minutes each, then set aside.
Stir-fry the broccoli and pepper for 3 minutes with a splash of water. Add the garlic, ginger, edamame and most of the spring onions for 1 minute.
Return the beef, pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute until glossy.
Plate using the plating guide. Scatter with sesame seeds and the remaining spring onions.
reheat_note: Microwave for 2 minutes until piping hot. Add a splash of water to the noodles before reheating.

title: Chicken souvlaki with Greek salad and tzatziki

shared.note: half grated for tzatziki, half diced

flexible.cook_note: Toast pittas; for bulgur, pour boiling water over and cover for 15 min.

steps: Mix the chicken with half the lemon juice, the oregano, garlic, half the oil and a pinch of salt. Leave for 5 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).
Thread onto skewers if you like. Cook under a hot grill or in the air fryer at 200C for 12-15 minutes, turning once, until cooked through.
Tzatziki: mix the yoghurt with the grated, squeezed cucumber, the mint and a pinch of salt.
Salad: toss the lettuce, tomatoes, diced cucumber, red onion, olives and chickpeas with the remaining oil and lemon juice. Top with the feta.
Plate using the plating guide with pitta or bulgur.
reheat_note: Good cold. Or microwave the chicken for 1-2 minutes. Keep the salad and tzatziki separate.

title: Harissa turkey meatballs with chickpeas and lemony yoghurt

flexible.cook_note: Couscous: pour over boiling water, cover for 5 min, then fluff.

steps: Mix the turkey, egg, breadcrumbs, 1 tbsp harissa, the cumin, half the garlic and a pinch of salt. Roll into about 20 meatballs.
Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan and brown the meatballs all over for 5 minutes. Set aside.
In the same pan, soften the onion, pepper and courgette for 5 minutes. Add the remaining garlic and harissa for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas, return the meatballs, cover and simmer for 12-15 minutes until cooked through. Stir in the spinach to wilt.
Mix the yoghurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Plate using the plating guide with a dollop of lemony yoghurt and the parsley.
reheat_note: Microwave for 2-3 minutes until piping hot. Pack the yoghurt separately.

title: Chicken and red lentil dhal with spinach

shared.display: 1 cube, made up with 700 ml water

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan. Soften the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir to coat in the spices for 2 minutes.

Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and the chicken is cooked. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then the lemon juice. Season to taste.
Split using the plating guide. Top with yoghurt and coriander.
reheat_note: Microwave for 3 minutes with a splash of water, stirring halfway, until piping hot. Freezes well.

title: Gochujang pork with edamame and quick-pickled cucumber

flexible.cook_note: Boil brown basmati for 25 min; microwave cauliflower rice for 3 min.

steps: Toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt. Set aside to pickle.
Start the rice if you're having it.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok over a high heat. Fry the pork for 6-8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and a little crispy.
Add the garlic, ginger and carrots for 2 minutes, then stir in the gochujang, soy sauce and 3 tbsp water.
Add the edamame and spinach and cook for 2-3 minutes until hot and wilted. Stir in most of the spring onions.
Plate using the plating guide, topped with the pickled cucumber, sesame seeds and the remaining spring onions.
reheat_note: Microwave for 2-3 minutes until piping hot. Pack the pickled cucumber separately.

title: Turkey and lentil bolognese

shared.display: 1 cube, made up with 300 ml water

flexible.cook_note: Cook pasta per the pack (10-12 min); fry courgetti in a hot pan for 2 min.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan. Soften the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Turn up the heat and brown the turkey mince for 5 minutes, breaking it up.
Stir in the tomato puree, then the lentils, tomatoes, stock and oregano.
Simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have melted into the sauce. Season to taste.
Cook your chosen pasta or courgetti near the end.
Plate using the plating guide, topped with torn basil and grated parmesan.
reheat_note: Microwave for 3 minutes, stirring halfway, until piping hot. The sauce freezes well; store pasta and sauce together for lunches.

title: Creamy Tuscan chicken with butter beans and spinach

shared.display: 1 cube, made up with 250 ml water

flexible.cook_note: Cook pasta per the pack (10-12 min); steam tenderstem for 4 min.

steps: Season the chicken with the oregano, salt and pepper. Start the pasta if you're having it.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the chicken for 4-5 minutes each side until golden and cooked through. Set aside.
Add the garlic, sun-dried tomatoes and cherry tomatoes to the pan for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock, then stir in the soft cheese and parmesan until smooth. Add the butter beans and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the spinach to wilt. Slice the chicken and return it to the sauce.
Plate using the plating guide.
reheat_note: Microwave for 2-3 minutes, stirring halfway, with a splash of water to loosen the sauce.

title: Crispy tofu satay stir-fry with edamame

flexible.cook_note: Cook noodles per the pack (about 5 min); boil brown basmati for 25 min.

steps: Air-fry the tofu cubes at 200C for 15 minutes, shaking halfway, until crisp. (Or roast at 220C for 25 minutes.)
Satay sauce: whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, garlic, ginger, chilli and 4-5 tbsp hot water until smooth.
Cook the noodles or rice if you're having them.
Heat the sesame oil in a wok. Stir-fry the broccoli, pepper and carrot for 4 minutes with a splash of water, then add the edamame for 2 minutes.
Add the tofu and satay sauce and toss until coated. Stir in most of the spring onions.
Plate using the plating guide, topped with the remaining spring onions.
reheat_note: Microwave for 2 minutes with a splash of water. The tofu softens a little but stays tasty.

title: Paneer, chickpea and lentil saag

shared.display: 1 cube, made up with 500 ml water
300 g (half stirred in, half to serve)

flexible.cook_note: Boil brown basmati for 25 min; microwave cauliflower rice for 3 min.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the paneer cubes until golden on a few sides, about 4 minutes. Set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock. Simmer for 15 minutes until the lentils are soft. Start the rice if you're having it.
Add the chickpeas, edamame and spinach a handful at a time until wilted. Return the paneer for 2 minutes.
Take off the heat and stir in half the yoghurt and the lemon juice. Season.
Plate using the plating guide with the remaining yoghurt on top.
reheat_note: Microwave for 2-3 minutes, stirring halfway, until piping hot. Add the yoghurt topping after reheating.

title: Jerk chicken with coconut kidney beans and lime slaw

flexible.cook_note: Boil brown basmati for 25 min; microwave cauliflower rice for 3 min.

steps: Heat the oven to 220C (200C fan). Rub the chicken with the jerk seasoning, half the lime juice and half the oil.
Roast on a lined tray for 25-30 minutes until cooked through and charred. Start the rice if you're having it.
Meanwhile heat the rest of the oil in a pan. Soften the garlic and most of the spring onions for 2 minutes, then add the kidney beans and coconut milk and simmer for 8 minutes until creamy. Season.
Slaw: toss the cabbage and carrot with the yoghurt, the remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Slice the chicken and plate using the plating guide: carb, then the coconut beans, chicken and slaw. Finish with coriander and the remaining spring onions.
reheat_note: Microwave the chicken, beans and rice for 2-3 minutes until piping hot. Pack the slaw separately.

title: Chicken shawarma bowls with houmous and tahini dressing

flexible.cook_note: Rinse quinoa and simmer for 15 min; warm pittas in the toaster.

steps: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, spices, garlic, 1 tbsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Start the quinoa if you're having it.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over a high heat. Cook the chicken and red onion for 8-10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and charred at the edges.
Dressing: whisk the tahini with the rest of the lemon juice, a pinch of salt and 2-3 tbsp water until pourable.
Build bowls: lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes and chickpeas, then the chicken, a spoonful of houmous, the dressing and parsley. Add the carb per the plating guide.
reheat_note: Good cold. To eat warm, microwave the chicken and quinoa only for 1-2 minutes. Pack the salad and dressing separately.

title: Cajun turkey burgers with sweet potato wedges and slaw

shared.note: smashed with a pinch of salt

flexible.cook_note: Cut sweet potato into wedges and air-fry at 200C for 20 min (or roast at 220C for 30 min).

steps: Toss the sweet potato wedges with a little of the oil and roast or air-fry (see the carb note).
Mix the turkey, Cajun seasoning, grated onion, egg and a pinch of salt. Shape into 8 patties.
Brush the patties with the rest of the oil. Grill, air-fry or pan-fry for 5-6 minutes each side until cooked through.
Slaw: toss the cabbage and carrot with the yoghurt, lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Plate using the plating guide: 2 patties each (or as the split suggests), with lettuce, tomatoes, smashed avocado and slaw.
reheat_note: Microwave the patties and wedges for 2 minutes, or re-crisp in the air fryer for 4 minutes. Pack the slaw and avocado separately (squeeze lime over the avocado).

title: Crispy breaded cod with chips, minted peas and yoghurt tartare

flexible.cook_note: Cut into chips, toss with a little oil and air-fry at 200C for 20-25 min, shaking twice.

steps: Start the chips (see the carb note).
Mix the breadcrumbs with the parsley, half the oil and a pinch of salt. Dip each cod loin in egg, then press into the crumbs.
Air-fry the cod at 200C for 10-12 minutes (or bake at 220C for 15 minutes) until golden and the fish flakes.
Cook the peas in boiling water for 3 minutes. Drain and roughly crush with the mint, the rest of the oil and a squeeze of lemon.
Tartare: mix the yoghurt with the capers, gherkins and the rest of the lemon juice.
Plate using the plating guide.
reheat_note: Best eaten fresh. If you make 4 portions, chill the cod and chips and re-crisp in the air fryer for 5-6 minutes. Don't microwave.

title: Slow-cooked lamb rogan josh with spinach

flexible.cook_note: Boil brown basmati for 25 min; microwave cauliflower rice for 3 min.

steps: Heat the oil in a casserole and brown the lamb in batches. Set aside.
Lower the heat and cook the onions for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute, then the tomato puree.
Return the lamb with the tomatoes and 200 ml water. Cover and simmer gently for 60 minutes (or slow-cook on low for 6 hours) until tender.
Take off the heat and stir in the yoghurt a spoonful at a time, then the chickpeas. Simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Stir in the spinach to wilt. Cook the rice while it finishes.
Plate using the plating guide with coriander on top.
reheat_note: Microwave for 3 minutes, stirring halfway, until piping hot. Even better the next day. Freezes well.

title: Sirloin steak with chimichurri, garlicky butter beans and tenderstem

flexible.cook_note: Cut into fries and air-fry at 200C for 20 min, shaking twice.

steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking. Start the fries (see the carb note).
Chimichurri: mix the parsley, a third of the garlic, the vinegar, oregano, chilli flakes, 2 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt.
Warm 1/2 tbsp oil in a pan with the rest of the garlic, add the butter beans and a splash of water and cook for 5 minutes, lightly crushing some of the beans. Season.
Steam or griddle the tenderstem for 4 minutes. Blister the tomatoes in a hot pan for 3 minutes.
Rub the steaks with the remaining oil and season. Cook in a very hot pan for 2-3 minutes each side for medium-rare. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Plate using the plating guide and spoon over the chimichurri.
reheat_note: Best fresh. Leftover steak is good cold, sliced over the beans.

title: Chicken, chickpea and olive tagine

shared.display: 1 cube, made up with 300 ml water

flexible.cook_note: Couscous: pour over boiling water, cover for 5 min, then fluff.

steps: Heat the oil in a large casserole and brown the chicken all over. Set aside.
Soften the onions for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Return the chicken with the tomatoes, stock, chickpeas and carrots. Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
Add the courgette and olives and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Stir in the lemon juice and zest. Season. Make the couscous.
Plate using the plating guide with coriander on top.
reheat_note: Microwave for 3 minutes, stirring halfway, until piping hot. Freezes well, and makes a great Monday lunch from a Sunday cook.
